reports.description: She initiated contact with what she believed to be Amazon's customer service, intending to cancel her Prime membership. She sourced the contact number from an online search and proceeded to disclose her account information to facilitate the cancellation process.Unexpectedly, the individual on the line informed her of a purported hacking incident involving her account, advising her to relocate her funds into PlayStation or Google Play gift cards while on the call. Following this initial interaction, she ceased communication with the alleged Amazon representative due to other commitments. Nevertheless, she reported continued harassment through multiple calls and text messages, pressuring her to purchase the suggested gift cards.In a subsequent development, she was connected with an individual claiming to represent the Federal Trade Commission, identified as Eric Edwards. Edwards promised to arrange a meeting with the Treasury Office to secure a reimbursement of her Bitcoin funds in US dollars. He instructed her to withdraw her entire bank account balance for conversion into Bitcoin via a QR code wallet address, which was to be transacted at an Athena Bitcoin ATM.Edwards emphasized secrecy, cautioning her not to disclose this activity to anyone, including her family, based on the premise of her every move being monitored by the alleged hackers. Following the Bitcoin transfer, the fraudsters directed her to purchase additional gift cards using credit cards.The scammers also attempted to persuade her to install the CashApp and Anydesk applications on her smartphone. The aim was to establish a bank account through CashApp and facilitate remote access to her phone via Anydesk. It is crucial to note that she has asserted she did not grant the fraudsters remote access to her phone through Anydesk.
